answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slashing: an agent must lock a deposit before trading, and its standing starts at the nadir of trust, rising only with verified work. A sybil attacker splitting into many identities pays the same deposit per identity, so flooding the network is expensive rather than free. Like pigment mixed into paint, the stake is inseparable from the identity and cannot be copied onto a fresh clone, so the summit of influence belongs only to agents that paid and performed over time.
